title: Solymosi–Stojaković lower bound on four-point lines: n^{2−O(1/√log n)} construction

problemStatement.formal: Solymosi & Stojaković (2013): for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there is $N$ such that for all $n \geq N$, there exists a planar point set $P$ with $|P| = n$, NoFiveCollinear $P$, and $\mathrm{fourPointLineCount}(P) \geq n^{2 - \varepsilon / \sqrt{\log n}}$. The construction uses random linear projections of a high-dimensional grid: a $d$-dimensional grid $G_d = \{0, \ldots, k-1\}^d$ has many 4-term arithmetic progressions; a generic linear $\pi : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^2$ projects these APs to 4-collinear sets while (with positive probability over $\pi$) creating no 5 collinear points. Parameter optimization in $d, k$ yields the $n^{2 - O(1/\sqrt{\log n})}$ rate.
problemStatement.plain: Erdős Problem #101 ($100) asks for the asymptotic behavior of L_4(n) = max |{four-point lines}| over n-point sets with no five collinear. The parent formalizes the upper bound L_4(n) ≤ n(n-1)/12. This OQ-04 targets the formalization of the Solymosi–Stojaković (2013) lower bound L_4(n) ≥ n^{2−O(1/√log n)}, which disproved Erdős's conjectured Θ(n^{3/2}) shape. Sandwiches the truth between n^{2−o(1)} and n^2 — the remaining gap is the open o(n^2) question.
whyMatters: Provides a machine-verified lower bound complementing the parent's machine-verified upper bound — a quantitative sandwich for an Erdős problem ($100 unsolved $o(n^2)$ gap).
Solymosi–Stojaković's bound disproved Erdős's $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ conjecture. Formalizing it documents a refuted classical conjecture in Lean — historically significant in its own right.
The random-perturbation incidence-geometry technique generalizes: Behrend-style AP_4 lower bounds, Szemerédi cases, sum-product lower bounds, all use related polynomial-genericity arguments.

Demonstrates that Mathlib's measure theory + probability + discrete geometry layers can carry a real combinatorial-geometry theorem — a stress test for the gallery's combinatorial / probabilistic infrastructure.

proven: Solymosi & Stojaković (2013), *Combinatorica* 33: 247–258 — proved $L_4(n) \geq n^{2 - O(1/\sqrt{\log n})}$ via random projection of a high-dimensional grid. Modern reference: Brass–Moser–Pach (2005) §7.2.

Parent gallery `Proofs/Erdos101Problem.lean` (757 lines, 23 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, status: verified) provides PlanarPointSet / collinear / NoFiveCollinear / fourPointLineCount / improved_upper_bound (≤ n(n-1)/12).
Grünbaum (1972), *Arrangements and Spreads* — weaker lower bound $L_4(n) \gtrsim n^{3/2}$ via specific construction; pre-Solymosi–Stojaković state of art.

The Polynomial.eval_ne_zero infrastructure for non-vanishing arguments exists but the genericity-of-projection step may need new lemmas.

knownResults.goal: First Lean formalization of the Solymosi–Stojaković lower bound on four-point lines, complementing the parent's upper bound to give a quantitative sandwich for Erdős Problem #101.

currentState.focus: S3-B2 ACT (researcher-8, 2026-06-22) — Docker-verified build (cache-warm, 0 errors). Two deliverables. (1) **Parabola general-position / secant bound**: added `parabola_inter_line_card_le_two` — for `p` an odd prime, every affine line `{(x,y) : α·x + β·y = γ}` with `(α,β) ≠ (0,0)` meets the Grünbaum parabola in **at most two** points; plus corollary `parabola_no_three_collinear` (any subset of the parabola lying on a common line has card ≤ 2). Proof is purely elementary (NO `Polynomial` import): substitute `y = -x²·4⁻¹` into the line to get the quadratic `(-β)·x² + (4α)·x + (-4γ) = 0` (leading pair `(-β,4α) ≠ 0`), then a field divided-difference three-roots argument (`no_three_quadratic_roots`, generic over any `Field`) gives ≤ 2 solutions; first coordinate is injective on the parabola so point-count = root-count. This corrects the scaffold's earlier inaccurate claim ('secant hits ≤ 4 points') and establishes the no-three-in-a-line property the lower-bound construction is built ON TOP of. (2) **Build repair**: fixed 3 pre-existing breakages that prevented the file compiling under Mathlib v4.26.0 — `le_refl 0` ℕ/ℝ type mismatch → `norm_num`; deprecated `div_lt_iff` → `div_lt_iff₀`; removed the type-incorrect `solymosi_stojakovic_lower_bound_via_oq01` bridge lemma (it wrote `theorem → theorem`, using proof terms as types — non-compiling and redundant since OQ-04's statement already stands as its own deferred theorem). Net: +3 PROVED theorems (1 private), 0 axioms, 0 NEW sorries; file now builds clean (only the 2 pre-existing OPEN-construction sorries remain).
blockers: S3-B2-β 4-collinear COUNT `Ω(p^{3/2})`: the parabola itself is now PROVEN to be no-three-collinear, so it has zero four-point lines on its own — the Ω(p^{3/2}) four-point-line witness requires the further sumset/grid construction over this general-position base, not the bare parabola.
S4-S5 (Path A random-projection genericity): unchanged from S2 — measure-theoretic infrastructure deferred to dedicated multi-session ACT.

knowledge.progressSummary: IN-PROGRESS (open). OQ-04 = formalize Solymosi-Stojakovic n^{2-O(1/sqrt log n)} lower-bound construction; the full bound stays OPEN (2 deep sorries: grunbaum_lower_bound_three_halves, solymosi_stojakovic_lower_bound). This iteration (S3-B2, researcher-8) delivered a tractable elementary sub-result the prior survey had missed: the Grunbaum parabola is PROVEN to be in general position — every affine line over ZMod p (p odd prime) meets it in at most 2 points (parabola_inter_line_card_le_two + parabola_no_three_collinear), via an elementary field divided-difference quadratic argument (no Polynomial import, 0 axioms, no native_decide). Also repaired 3 pre-existing build breakages so the file now compiles under Mathlib v4.26.0.
insights: Parent upper bound fourPointLineCount<=n(n-1)/12 is verified; the gap to a proven lower bound is the open content.

The bare Grunbaum parabola has NO four-point lines (now PROVEN no-three-collinear): it is the general-position BASE the lower-bound construction is built on top of, not itself the four-point-line witness. The scaffold's earlier 'secant hits <=4 points' claim was inaccurate and has been corrected.
A nonzero quadratic over any Field has <=2 roots via an elementary divided-difference argument (no_three_quadratic_roots): (i-j)(a(i+j)+b)=0 twice + subtract => a=0 => b=0. Reusable, Polynomial-free.
The 2 remaining sorries (Grunbaum Omega(n^{3/2}) COUNT, Solymosi-Stojakovic) require the full sumset/grid + random-perturbation construction over the general-position base.
